parsed.explanation: The text defines v(B) via the decreasing order |...||b1-b2|-b3|...|, while Lemma 4.1 only produces SOME ordering of P∪N with nested difference g. The objector's example is correct: for P={8,7,5}, N={10,9} the sums 20,19 differ by 1 and no subset sum lies strictly between (all integers), so 4.1(b) applies, yet the decreasing order 10,9,8,7,5 gives |10-9|=1, |1-8|=7, |7-7|=0, |0-5|=5. So the step as stated (decreasing-order chain value ≤ g) does not follow; Theorem 4.2's conclusion is proved only for some ordering. But this is a notational mismatch, not a substantive gap: XY's strategy processes b_1,...,b_r sequentially, cutting 'the larger of the two pieces {v_run,b_k}', which is order-agnostic and yields final running value equal to the nested difference in whatever order is used. Applying it in Lemma 4.1's order gives D=g≤T_n. Upper bound survives.
